text:
Situation: Fentanyl citrate injection remains on FDA's shortage list for Hospira, Inc. (initial posting 2012-01-01, update 2026-10-08), Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC (initial posting 2012-01-01, update 2026-10-15), and Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Inc. (initial posting 2023-12-20, update 2026-10-14). Corvale East holds 5.6 days of 1 mL syringes and 7–8 days of 2 mL vials. Corvale General holds 18 days across both presentations. Corvale Lakeside holds 17.3 days of 2 mL vials.

Why (FDA record): FDA's database shows the shortage as current since 2012-01-01 for Hospira and Fresenius Kabi, and since 2023-12-20 for Hikma, with updates through mid-October 2026. The earliest posting is 2012-01-01, so the shortage began on or before that date and no gap is measured from it.

Our position: We have Hikma-labeled 1 mL syringes (NDC 00641624810, plant FEI 2220525, last inspected NAI 2026-05-13) and Hospira-labeled 2 mL vials (NDC 00409909422, plant FEI 1021343, last inspected NAI 2025-02-07). Hospira's plant had OAI classifications after inspections ending 2010-01-19, 2011-06-17, and 2011-08-04, and a Warning Letter dated 2010-04-12, but the most recent inspection was NAI in 2025. Hikma's plant has shown only VAI or NAI classifications from 2009 through 2024, with the latest NAI in 2026.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 74 syringes of 50 mcg/mL 1 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — requires pharmacy director approval and a DEA Form 222 or CSOS order for Schedule II.
2. Transfer 154 vials of 50 mcg/mL 2 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — requires pharmacy director approval and a DEA Form 222 or CSOS order for Schedule II.
3. Evaluate purchase from Civica, Inc. — not on FDA's shortage list today; label names no plant we could place — requires buyer approval.
4. Evaluate purchase from Phlow Corp. — not on FDA's shortage list today; label names no plant we could place — requires buyer approval.
5. Use Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. 50 mcg/mL as alternate manufacturer — requires pharmacist verification; approved by Casey Nguyen, MD on 2026-02-28; FDA lists this product Current (posted 2023-12-20).

Not recommended: No clinical dosing or protocol changes; those are for treating clinicians and the committee.
